ui.title: How fast can you find it?
ui.intro: A short study on how the language of a written clue changes visual search. It takes no more than 15 minutes.
ui.demo_banner: Demo only. This study is awaiting ethics approval, and nothing recorded here is research data.
ui.consent_body: You will look at pictures and click on a target as quickly as you can, using a written clue. We record your clicks, timings, and answers to a short questionnaire. We never ask for your name, email, or location. You can stop at any time by closing the page. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must have given permission before you take part.
ui.education_years: Total years of education, counting from first grade
ui.years_reading_images: Years of experience reading medical images (0 if none)
ui.l2_age: Age when you started learning that other language
ui.instr_search: Busy pictures: the clue names a small object to find, and it is different every time.
ui.instr_scan: Grayscale medical images: something in each one is out of the ordinary. Find it and click on it. The two kinds of picture are mixed together.
ui.instr_dice: Grids with two dice: the clue tells you which way to move from the star, and the dice tell you how far. Click the square where you end up.
ui.instr_clue: Above each picture is a clue telling you what to look for and where. Read every clue carefully: it changes each time, sometimes in {l1} and sometimes in {l2}. Then click the target as fast as you can.
ui.instr_effort: After each picture, rate how much mental effort it took.
ui.instr_practice: The first picture of each kind is practice.
ui.effort_q: How much mental effort did that take?
ui.difficulty_q: Overall, how difficult was this study? (1 = very easy, 9 = very difficult)
ui.attention_q: To show you were reading carefully: which of these did you search for in a busy picture?
ui.debrief_body: This study asks whether reading a clue in your less comfortable language slows down visual search, whether that changes over the session, and whether experience and education change it. The very first image also tested something else: when your attention is on one job (finding the ring), do you notice something unexpected (the gorilla)? Many people, including experts, do not. We are testing whether the clue's language changes that.
ui.surprise_body: In the next image, find the small white ring and click on it. A written clue above the image tells you where to look.
ui.notice_q: Did you notice anything unusual in that image?
ui.gorilla_q: Did you see a gorilla in that image?
ui.knew_q: Before today, had you heard of the "invisible gorilla" study, where people miss a gorilla hidden in an image?
ui.instr_reveal: Thank you. There was a small gorilla in that image; many people miss it, and that is part of what we study. Nothing else in the study is a trick.
ui.instr_rounds: The pictures come in short rounds. Work quickly but carefully. The study stops by itself before 15 minutes, wherever you are; you do not need to finish every round.
ui.quit_confirm: Finish the picture part now and go to the last two questions?
ui.instr_quit: If you feel exhausted, use the "I'm exhausted" button under any picture. That is completely fine, and it helps the study.
ui.already_done: This session is complete. Thank you for taking part.
ui.bg_l1: Which language are you most comfortable reading?
ui.bg_l2: Which other language can you also read?
ui.bg_l1_reading: How well do you read your most comfortable language? (1 = very little, 7 = like a native speaker)
ui.bg_l2_reading: How well do you read that other language? (1 = very little, 7 = like a native speaker)
ui.fatigue_q: How mentally tired do you feel right now?
ui.bg_equal: I am equally comfortable reading both languages
ui.instr_corsi: Squares that light up: watch the order, then click them the way the clue says, in the same order or in reverse.
ui.instr_reading: Short passages: read the passage and choose the best answer.

search_leads: Somewhere there is a {np}. Click it.
scan_leads: Something in this image is out of the ordinary. Find it.
One thing here does not belong. Click on it.
Look for anything that does not match the rest of the image.
There is something unusual in this image.
where: It is in the {region} area of the image, closer to the {near} edge than to the {far} edge.
Check the {region} part, nearer the {near} edge than the {far} edge.
Search the {region} area; it sits closer to the {near} edge than to the {far} edge.
dice_leads: Start at the star. Move {dir_a} as many squares as die A shows, then {dir_b} as many as die B shows. Click where you end up.
From the star, go {dir_a} by the number on die A, then {dir_b} by the number on die B, and click that square.
Begin on the star: die A says how many squares to move {dir_a}, then die B says how many to move {dir_b}. Click the final square.

corsi.forward: Watch the squares light up one by one. Then click them in the same order.
corsi.backward: Watch the squares light up one by one. Then click them in reverse order, starting with the last one.
